Lessons.Title: More Practice to Represent and Solve
ExplanationParagraphs: The focus of the original 2021 lesson is Information Gap (MLR4): students request MISSING information needed to solve a multi-step problem, justify each request, and communicate how the quantities combine. This is not a general rounding worksheet.

Warm-up — Number Talk: Two Steps (10 minutes). The four original expressions are20+(2×3)=26,30+(4×3)=42,50+(8×3)=74 and99+(8×3)=123. Multiply the equal groups first and then add the starting quantity.

Activity 1 — Info Gap: Introduction (15 minutes). The original teacher source uses a chairs-in-a-room situation. Information needed includes how many chairs are in a corner, how many are in each row and how many rows. The problem-card holder asks, explains WHY each answer is needed; data card holder only shares numbers actually on the card. Teacher controls the original inaccessible image card values.

An INDEPENDENT Edulytics chairs demonstration, not original publisher card: 3 rows×6 chairs per row and4 in the corner. Asked correctly, the total becomes 3×6+4=22. Model it with multiplication followed by addition, but do not describe22 as a verified original-source numerical result.

Activity 2 — Info Gap: Bake Sale (20 minutes). The 2021 lesson has publisher picture-only problem/data cards. Their exact numbers are not present in the archived readable student text. The teacher supplies originals where licensed/available, or clearly switches to an independent first-party task while preserving the conversational mathematics.

First-party Bake Sale alternative: 5 trays of8 muffins with13 additional muffins. Only the data-card student initially sees the number of trays, muffins per tray and extra muffins. Other pupil must explain the data needed, then solve 5×8+13=53. The source publisher's precise figures and gated Reflection are NOT represented as known or copied.

After solving, reverse roles, get another set of cards, compare methods and justify why the information was necessary. A scalar score cannot measure precision of questions, respectful listening, turn-taking, or independently reasoned steps; these need teacher review.

KeyConcepts.Title: Information Gap
KeyConcepts.Definition: Different students hold a problem and supporting data, requiring mathematical questions to assemble the full model.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Ask for only facts needed; justify before receiving; solve and compare after sufficient data.
KeyConcepts.Example: Rows, chairs per row and extra chairs.

KeyConcepts.Title: Two-step multi-group expression
KeyConcepts.Definition: Multiply equal groups, then add or subtract a separate quantity.

KeyConcepts.Title: Source provenance
KeyConcepts.Definition: A first-party model can demonstrate the skill without being identical to restricted publisher cards.
KeyConcepts.Rule: Never claim a publisher image-only value was verified from alt text alone.
KeyConcepts.Example: Independent bake task5×8+13=53 versus unknown original source data.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent chairs information gap
WorkedExamples.Question: 3 rows of6 chairs plus4 in a corner: total?
WorkedExamples.Method: Ask for rows and chairs per row and extra chairs.
Steps: Need row count3, chairs in each row6, chairs in corner4.
WorkedExamples.Check: This scenario is not the exact 2021 publisher card.

WorkedExamples.Title: Independent Bake Sale data card
WorkedExamples.Question: Five trays hold eight muffins each and thirteen more are loose. How many?
Steps: Ask how many muffins per tray:8.
WorkedExamples.Check: All numbers are first-party, not copied from original card image.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Fabricate a source Bake Sale card number from absent figure pixels.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Alt text does not disclose actual teacher card data.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Use original teacher card under teacher control or an independently authored card with explicit provenance.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Ask the data-card partner for the answer.
CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: The source protocol requires explaining what data are needed and computing independently.
CommonMistakes.Correction: Ask for rows, items per row and separate quantities.

CommonMistakes.Mistake: Add before multiplication in expressions such as20+2×3.

SummaryPoints: 2021 routine: request, justify, receive only known data, solve, swap roles.
Publisher's Bake Sale card numbers and gated original reflection are unknown—not fabricated.
Teacher reviews mathematical discourse and representations.
